advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Give the `checkout-index` call in `_apply_delta` a timeout (or route it through `git_run`) so a stalled child falls closed instead of hanging.
evidence: delta_tree.py:240 `proc = run_git(repo_root, "checkout-index", ...)` — direct run_git call, no timeout arg
git_fetch.py:127-138 `git_run(...)` wraps `run_git(..., timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT)` and returns returncode 124 on TimeoutExpired
gitutil.py:125 `timeout: float | None = None` — run_git defaults to no timeout, and `_apply_delta` does not pass one
advisory.finding: _apply_delta runs `checkout-index` via `run_git` with no timeout, whereas every other git invocation in delta_tree.py goes through `git_run` which applies `_GIT_TIMEOUT` and synthesizes a failed result on TimeoutExpired. A hung/blocked checkout-index (e.g. terminal prompt despite GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, or FS stall) blocks the whole materialization indefinitely instead of falling closed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Pass `timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT` to the run_git call in _apply_delta and treat TimeoutExpired as a False (fail-closed) result, matching git_run's contract.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Close the st_nlink TOCTOU: compute the exclusive_size/link-count delta and apply it to bytes.total under a single serialization so concurrent populate/evict of a shared inode cannot both observe st_nlink>1 and skip accounting it.
evidence: Shared mutable resource: the running byte total 'bytes.total' and, underlying it, a hardlinked blob inode shared between a donor entry and a newly built entry — cache.py:263 populate credits `add_bytes(exclusive_size(dest), root)` and janitor.py:214 evict applies `_cache.add_bytes(-size, root)` where `size = _cache.exclusive_size(entry)` (janitor.py:205).

Two concurrent executors: populate under the per-SHA lock `with interprocess_lock(_sha_lock_path(root, sha))` (cache.py:257) and the janitor's `_evict` under the SEPARATE GC interlock flock `fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)` (janitor.py:344). Different lock resources ⇒ populate of X and eviction of neighbour D overlap.

Sibling accessor + guard: `add_bytes` serializes ONLY the counter — 'with interprocess_lock(root / "locks" / "bytes.total.lock")' (cache.py:119), docstring 'no read-modify-write TOCTOU' (cache.py:116). The st_nlink read that produces the delta is NOT inside that lock.

Interleaving window (read/read of mutable state): unlocked READ in exclusive_size — `st = os.lstat(...)` then `if st.st_nlink == 1: total += st.st_size` (cache.py:145,153-154) — executed by BOTH the populate of X and the concurrent `_evict(D)` on the same shared blob B while B has st_nlink==2. The interleaved WRITE is `_evict` removing D's link via `os.rename(entry, dest)` then `shutil.rmtree(dest, ...)` (janitor.py:209,212), which drops B to st_nlink==1 AFTER both size measurements were taken.

Concrete harm (lost update / corrupted invariant): populate saw st_nlink==2 for B and did not add it (assuming D accounts it); concurrent _evict saw st_nlink==2 for B and did not subtract it (assuming the survivor accounts it). After both complete B has one link but was never added to bytes.total — the incremental total permanently UNDER-counts real disk. The reverse ordering (both count) OVER-counts. Either way byte_total diverges from distinct_bytes, so the max_bytes cap (janitor.py:428 `over_budget = ... used > cfg.max_bytes`) acts on a figure that no longer describes the disk — the exact class of bug this ticket set out to fix.
advisory.finding: The incremental byte-total accounting reads st_nlink in exclusive_size() outside the bytes.total serialization, so a populate of one entry and a concurrent janitor eviction of a hardlink neighbour can both observe the same shared inode as st_nlink>1 and each decline to charge/credit it — breaking the 'each inode added once and subtracted once' invariant the design depends on.
scenarios: A gate resolution populates tickets-<shaX> by hardlinking donor tickets-<shaD> at the same moment a janitor process in another replica evicts tickets-<shaD> under disk pressure.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a tickets tree containing a symlink/gitlink declines the delta path and full-materializes a faithful, byte-matching entry.
evidence: delta_tree.py: `if mode not in _LINKABLE_MODES or not path: return None`
delta_tree.py: `if src.is_symlink(): return False  # os.link would dereference it`
search of tests/ for 'symlink' in test_repo_snapshot.py returned (no matches)
Commit message: 'a symlink or gitlink ... falls back to the unchanged full materialization' — a faithfulness claim with no regression test
advisory.finding: The symlink/gitlink fail-closed fallback in delta_tree.py has no test. `_tree_paths` returns None (and `_link_tree_paths` returns False) when a tree contains a symlink or gitlink, and the contract is that materialization then falls back to a full, faithful checkout. No test builds a tickets tree containing a symlink or submodule and asserts (a) the delta path declines and (b) the resulting entry still byte-matches the committed tree.
scenarios: A tickets tree gains a symlink or submodule; the delta path must decline and the full materialization must still produce a faithful tree

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that removes a committed path from a donor entry and asserts the delta build declines and the resulting entry byte-matches its SHA.
evidence: delta_tree.py docstring: 'a missing entry means the donor was partially evicted ... so we return False and the caller full-materializes'
delta_tree.py `_link_tree_paths`: `except OSError: return False  # Missing (donor partially evicted / incomplete)...`
search of tests/ for 'incomplete donor' and 'full materializ' returned (no matches) in the snapshot tests
advisory.finding: The 'incomplete / partially-evicted donor' fail-closed path is untested. The module documents that a donor can vanish mid-walk (janitor renames-then-rmtrees), so `_link_tree_paths` compares against `git ls-tree` and returns False on any missing path, and the caller full-materializes. No test injects a donor entry missing a committed path and asserts the delta path is abandoned and the new entry is still faithful.
scenarios: A donor entry is concurrently evicted mid-build, leaving some committed paths absent; the built entry must not be missing blobs

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a delta test where the changed commit deletes and renames files, asserting the built entry byte-matches the SHA (deleted paths absent, renamed dest present).
evidence: delta_tree.py `_diff_paths`: `width = 3 if status in ('R', 'C') else 2` and `elif status == 'D': deletes.add(tokens[i + 1])`
test_repo_snapshot.py only mutates existing files: `(tickets / f"t{i:03d}.json").write_text(payload[:-1] + "X")` — no add/delete/rename between adjacent SHAs
delta_tree.py `_prune_empty_dirs` and the `for rel in deletes` unlink loop are reachable only via a delete/rename delta
advisory.finding: Rename and delete deltas are never exercised. `_diff_paths` has dedicated two-token handling for rename/copy statuses and a `deletes` set, and `_apply_delta`/`_prune_empty_dirs` remove paths and empty dirs — yet every test builds deltas by rewriting a file in place, so `D`/`R` statuses, deletion pruning, and the two-token consumer are all untested. A real tickets commit routinely deletes or renames files.
scenarios: An adjacent tickets commit deletes or renames a file; the entry must contain exactly the new tree (deleted path gone, renamed dest present, empty dirs pruned)

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] After `_apply_delta` succeeds, assert the assembled path set equals `target_paths` and `_discard`+fall closed on any mismatch, rather than trusting git diff to be exhaustive.
evidence: delta_tree.py:296-299 links `donor_paths - deletes - writes` then applies `writes`; returns True on success with no check that the union == `target_paths`

delta_tree.py docstring lines 42-44 claim 'we compare what we cloned against git ls-tree -r and discard on any mismatch' — the code compares donor completeness via os.link failure only, not the final tree against target_paths
delta_tree.py:279 `target_paths = _tree_paths(repo_root, sha)` is computed but only used for `_unshareable`, never for a final completeness assertion
dropped.finding: materialize_via_donor never verifies that the assembled tree (linked paths + written paths) equals `target_paths`. Completeness is only enforced indirectly: `_link_tree_paths` fails when a donor path is missing, and `_apply_delta` writes `writes`. If `git diff` omits a path that genuinely differs (or the diff/ls-tree disagree on the target's path set), the entry is accepted as complete despite not byte-matching `git ls-tree -r <sha>`, contradicting the docstring's 'compare what we cloned against git ls-tree -r and discard on any mismatch' claim.
dropped.suggested_fix: Compute `linked = donor_paths - deletes - writes`; require `linked | writes == target_paths` (and that every write path is in target_paths) before returning True; otherwise _discard and continue to the next donor / full materialize.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm every `_evict` caller (including direct `reverify_entry` use) holds the GC interlock, or document/guard that concurrent eviction can transiently over-state the byte total until the next sweep.
evidence: cache.py:174 `if st.st_nlink == 1: total += st.st_size` — a blob shared by two entries being evicted concurrently is nlink==2 for both measurements
janitor.py:205 `_evict` measures `exclusive_size(entry)` BEFORE the rename, then `add_bytes(-size)`; two concurrent evictors of sibling sharers each under-count the shared inode
janitor.py:278 `reverify_entry` calls `_evict` and is a module-public function not itself taking the gc interlock (the interlock is held only when reached via _gc_pass/_reverify_pass)
dropped.finding: exclusive_size-based eviction accounting is only correct under serialized eviction; if `reverify_entry` (a public function whose `_evict` frees a corrupt entry) is invoked outside the GC interlock concurrently with a janitor pass, two evictors can each observe st_nlink==2 on a shared blob and both skip crediting it, so the freed bytes are never subtracted from the running total until the next startup_sweep reconciles.
